newsitem.title: USA: Ross-Bombing adds to Middle East difficulties.
newsitem.headline: Ross-Bombing adds to Middle East difficulties.

text.p: A fatal bombing in Tel Aviv on Friday added to the difficult circumstances around the Middle East peace process, but the process has weathered such shocks in the past, special U.S. envoy Dennis Ross said.
"There is obviously a difficult environment in which we're operating," Ross said in an interview on CNN. "... What is most important is efforts have to made to find a way to go forward."
The bombing in a Tel Aviv cafe left four people dead, including the suicide bomber, and 42 others injured.

Asked about the impact of Friday's attack on progress toward so-called "final status" issues in the peace talks, including complex questions like the fate of Jerusalem, Ross said, "It adds to the difficulty of the circumstances that we face.

"But I think one thing we have to bear in mind: this is a process that has endured a great deal, this is not unfortunately the first time we experienced shocks and trauma," he said. "This is a process that has experienced a lot and somehow it has endured."

Ross said the Hamas Islamic fundamentalist group bears responsibility for the attack and said that despite heated rhetoric by Israeli and Palestinian leaders in recent days, "I don't think that you can pin the responsibility on the leaders."
